newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ship operators to resume dividend -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan ship operators to resume dividend -- paper.

text.p: Major Japanese ship operators Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd, Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd and Navix Line Ltd will likely resume dividend payments in the year to end-March 1998, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported on Tuesday.
The companies will likely pay an annual dividend of three to four yen per share in 1997/98, the paper said.

The companies' business performances have improved as result of restructuring measures, including a cut in the number of Japanese sailors, and the weak yen, which boosted their international competitiveness.

Mitsui O.S.K. Lines is expected to see its parent current profit rise by 38 percent to 11 billion yen in 1997/98, while Navix Line will likely see its parent current profit increase three percent to 3.6 billion yen, the paper said.

A Navix Line spokesman said that the company cannot confirm that it will resume dividend payouts although it aims to do so as soon as possible. A spokesman for Mitsui O.S.K. Lines declined to comment on the report.
A spokesman for Kawasaki Kisen was not immediately available to comment.
